title: The signed fibre of a natural transformation of additive functors preserves cone triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $A,B:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be additive functors, and let $r:A\Rightarrow B$ be a natural transformation. Use integer cochain complexes, shifts and the cone convention $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=L^n\oplus K^{n+1}$, $d(x,y)=(d_Lx+f(y),-d_Ky)$, with boundary $-p$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a complex $I$ define $F(I)^n=A(I^n)\oplus B(I^{n-1})$ with differential $D(a,b)=(d_Aa,r(a)-d_Bb)$, and for a chain map $f:I\to J$ put $F(f)(a,b)=(A(f)a,B(f)b)$. These formulas induce an additive functor $F:K(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathrm{Ab})$ on homotopy categories. A homotopy $H$ between $f$ and $g$ induces the homotopy $(a,b)\mapsto(A(H)a,-B(H)b)$ between $F(f)$ and $F(g)$. The shift comparison $s_I:F(I[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(I)[1]$ is $(a,b)\mapsto(a,-b)$. For every $f:I\to J$, the formula
$$\Phi_f(x,y,z,w)=(x,z,y,-w)$$
in source order $A(J)^n\oplus A(I)^{n+1}\oplus B(J)^{n-1}\oplus B(I)^n$ and target order $F(J)^n\oplus F(I)^{n+1}$ is a natural chain isomorphism $F(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(F(f))$. It respects the inclusion of $F(J)$ and satisfies $s_I F(-p)=-p\Phi_f$. In particular $F$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with this shift comparison, and it restricts to bounded below complexes.
